item.title: An Adaptive Endmember-Corrected Mixing Model for Hyperspectral Unmixing
item.description: The linear mixing model (LMM) remains a widely used foundation for hyperspectral unmixing because of its simplicity and physical interpretability. In practical scenes, however, nonlinear (NL) interactions, endmember variability (EV), and other complex factors may cause the observed spectra to deviate from the LMM, resulting in model mismatch. Existing methods address model mismatch by introducing predefined NL or EV formulations, which may lack flexibility when the mismatch source is unknown or difficult to characterize. To address this issue, this article proposes an endmember-corrected mixing model that compensates for dominant mismatch-induced spectral deviations through a compact correction to the endmember representation. Specifically, an endmember correction term is introduced into the LMM and learned by an endmember residual correction network through self-supervised reconstruction of the observed hyperspectral image. Within the adopted additive correction structure, the endmember representation can adapt to the observed data without requiring prior identification of the underlying mismatch mechanism. Meanwhile, a deep image prior network is employed to generate spatially structured abundance maps. A two-stage optimization strategy is further adopted to reduce the coupling between endmember correction and abundance estimation, thereby improving the stability of the unmixing process. Experiments on synthetic and real hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves robust and competitive unmixing performance under different noise levels and model mismatch conditions.
item.authors: Jin-Ju Wang;Xi-Le Zhao;Jie Huang;Jia-Qing Miao;

item.title: Stable Feature Graph Similarity for Air–Ground Multiview 3-D Point Cloud Fusion Mapping in Confined Spaces
item.description: Uncrewed aerial vehicle-borne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is increasingly used for near-ground Earth observation and3-D geospatial data acquisition because of its rapid deployment and broad coverage. However, aerial platforms often provide sparse observations and may suffer from occlusion or limited accessibility in narrow, low-clearance, and obstacle-rich environments. Ground mobile platforms acquire denser close-range geometry but remain constrained by local occlusion, limited viewpoints, and poor visibility of elevated structures. Their complementary viewpoints therefore benefit confined-space mapping. Nevertheless, fusing heterogeneous air–ground point clouds remains challenging because differences in sensing height, viewpoint, field of view, point density, and spatial overlap make cross-platform place recognition and alignment unreliable. To address this problem, this article proposes an air–ground multiview point cloud fusion method based on stable feature graphs. Repeatable planar and high-intensity structures are extracted from LiDAR-inertial keyframe submaps to construct compact feature graphs. A graph similarity network, termed the graph-level interaction and subgraph cross-attention network, combines graph-level embedding interaction with label-specific subgraph cross-attention to identify overlapping regions between aerial and ground observations. Retrieved candidates are geometrically verified, and their relative poses are estimated using RANSAC and generalized iterative closest point registration. Verified cross-platform constraints are integrated with single-platform odometry through offline partitioned pose graph optimization to generate a globally consistent fused map. Experiments on multiple underground parking-garage sequences show that the proposed method improves cross-platform place-recognition performance by 16.6% over the second-best method, while also achieving better air–ground alignment, more complementary spatial coverage, and improved global map consistency.
item.authors: Haonan Chen;Kunhuang Liu;Xing Zhang;San Jiang;Qingquan Li;

item.title: SAR-to-Optical Translation Using Swin-U-DiT for Burned Area Mapping
item.description: Accurate and timely burned area mapping is critical for wildfire management and ecological assessment. Optical satellite sensors, such as Sentinel-2 MultiSpectral Instrument (MSI), provide well-suited data for this task but are often obstructed by clouds and smoke during and immediately after fire events. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) sensors offer all-weather imaging capabilities, but SAR data are challenging to interpret due to speckle noise and complex scattering mechanisms. This article introduces Swin-U-DiT, a conditional diffusion model designed to bridge this gap by translating SAR data into optical-like imagery. Our approach combines a U-Net backbone with efficient Transformer-based processing to generate high-fidelity optical equivalents from multitemporal Sentinel-1 SAR and prefire Sentinel-2 MSI data. It is more efficient than denoising diffusion probabilistic model architectures and performs better than GAN-based methods in the downstream task. We train and evaluate the model on a dataset comprising 2053 wildfire events across Canada during 2017–2022. The generated images enable downstream burned area mapping that achieves an F1-score of 0.8037. Given the rapidly increasing availability of SAR data, including RADARSAT constellation mission, NISAR, ICEYE, and other commercial constellations, this work offers strong promise for near-real-time burned area mapping in cloud-prone regions worldwide.
item.authors: Eric Brune;Yifang Ban;

item.title: ADST-Net: Adaptive Dual-Expert Refinement and Structure-Guided Temporal Modeling Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Remote sensing change detection aims to identify changed regions from bitemporal remote sensing images. Although deep learning-based methods have achieved remarkable progress, accurate detection remains challenging in complex scenes due to pseudochanges caused by imaging-condition variations, background texture disturbance, and insufficient structural consistency of bitemporal representations. To address these issues, this article proposes ADST-Net. The proposed network first refines single-temporal multiscale features through an adaptive dual-expert residual refinement module, which adaptively integrates local-detail modeling and large-kernel structural-context modeling before temporal comparison. Then, a structure-guided temporal difference modeling module organizes explicit temporal differences into more discriminative change representations. Finally, a progressive decoder reconstructs high-resolution binary change maps. On LEVIR-CD, SYSU-CD, and UAV-CD, ADST-Net achieves F1 scores of 91.71%, 83.93%, and 76.99%, respectively. These results, together with the ablation studies, indicate that the proposed refine-then-model strategy improves change detection accuracy while keeping the model lightweight.
item.authors: Yang Zhang;Jintao Xu;Yijun Zhou;

item.title: Graph and Attention-Based Convolutional Network for Polarimetric SAR Image Classification
item.description: In a polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification task, exploring polarimetric-spatial relationships among the given pixel with other classes is of high importance. Moreover, providing a rich source of global and local polarimetric, scattering, and contextual features is essential to achieve a high accurate classification map. To address these issues, a graph- and attention-based convolutional (GAC) network is designed in this work. To explore the relationships among the input patch with the mean patches of all classes, a graph branch with a correlation-based feature matrix and a learnable adjacency matrix is constructed, which leads to global feature extraction. To extract the relationships among the input patch with physical scattering characteristics of all classes, a cross-attention-based convolutional branch is designed to extract the local contextual features weighted by attended scattering properties. The extracted local and global features are finally fused and used for PolSAR image classification. The experimental results on synthetic and real benchmark datasets show superior performance of GAC with less number of model parameters compared to some state-of-the-art models.
item.authors: Maryam Imani;Sergio Escalera;

item.title: Deep Spectral Super-Resolution via Fourier Phase Prior and Spectral Degradation Guidance
item.description: Spectral super-resolution (SSR) aims to reconstruct high-fidelity hyperspectral images from low-resolution RGB or multispectral images. Existing methods often struggle to balance global spectral consistency and local spatial details, frequently overlooking the loss of structural information during reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose a deep SSR network via Fourier phase prior and spectral degradation guidance. By utilizing the half-quadratic splitting algorithm, we decouple the highly coupled objective function into three alternately optimized subproblems: spectral degradation and phase guidance, spectral low-rank projection, and deep prior, which are then unfolded into an end-to-end network. Specifically, the spectral degradation and phase guidance stage introduces a Fourier phase-amplitude mixing strategy, fusing the phase prior of the multispectral image with the feature amplitude from the previous stage. This enables the image reconstruction process to adhere to the spectral response function constraint while preserving clear structural contours. The spectral low-rank stage employs truncated singular value decomposition to project data into a low-dimensional clean subspace, effectively suppressing spectral distortion and noise. Furthermore, the deep prior stage adopts a dual-branch architecture. One branch, the bidirectional spectral fusion module, connects forward spectral multihead self-attention and backward multiscale 1-D convolutions in parallel, achieving comprehensive bidirectional mining of both global correlations and local details within the spectral sequence. The other branch utilizes orientation texture-aware attention, integrating learnable directional Gabor filters and coordinate features to precisely reconstruct the high-frequency texture structures of complex scenes. Experiments on natural and remote sensing datasets demonstrate that the proposed method effectively overcomes the limitations of single spatial–spectral mapping, achieving superior performance in both spatial texture recovery and spectral fidelity.
item.authors: Pengyue Zhang;Donge Zhao;Yayun Ma;Wenbo Chu;

item.title: Controlling Unreliable Observation Propagation in Satellite-Video Multiobject Tracking via Candidate Refinement and Short-Window Trajectory Rectification
item.description: High-resolution optical satellite video enables persistent wide-area observation. However, robust multiobject tracking remains highly challenging because small moving targets typically occupy only a few pixels and generate weak, temporally unstable responses that are easily confused with background clutter. Preserving such faint targets usually requires a recall-oriented strategy that retains low-confidence candidates. Once integrated into data association, these unreliable observations tend to propagate errors through matching and state updating, resulting in false trajectories, identity switches, and fragmentation. To address the conflict between weak-target preservation and unreliable-observation propagation, this article proposes a preserve–rectify–maintain tracking framework with two complementary components: weak-observation-oriented front-end refinement (WOFR) and spatio-temporal trajectory rectification and cascade tracking (STRC). A WOFR enhances target-background discriminability through representation-level temporal reweighting and improves response-map reliability through constrained heatmap correction, thereby improving candidate quality while retaining sensitivity to weak targets. An STRC implements trajectory-level rectification and maintenance by screening refined candidates through short-window global consistency reasoning, removing unsupported observations, and passing the rectified observations to a lightweight online tracker for efficient long-term association and state maintenance. By limiting the propagation of unreliable observations under weak-observation conditions, the proposed framework improves the balance between recall and tracking robustness. Experiments on the VISO and SATMTB-multiobject tracking (MOT) datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. On VISO, the method achieves 71.2% MOTA and 79.7% IDF1, outperforming the compared methods on both metrics. On SATMTB-MOT, it achieves the best MOTA and IDF1 for the airplane and car categories.
item.authors: Fen Hu;Peng Yang;Jie Dou;Lei Dou;

item.title: A Progressive Downscaling Framework With Hybrid Attention Mechanisms for High-Resolution Soil Moisture Estimation
item.description: Soil moisture is a critical variable regulating terrestrial water and energy exchange, with broad applications in drought monitoring, water resources management, and climate change research. However, passive microwave soil moisture products are often constrained by coarse spatial resolution, limiting their utility for regional- and local-scale applications. To address this challenge, we propose a progressive downscaling framework with hybrid attention mechanisms (PDHAM) to generate high-resolution soil moisture estimates. The framework progressively downscales soil moisture through two cascaded stages, first from 0.36° to 0.06° and then from 0.06° to 0.01°, thereby improving downscaling robustness. Each stage incorporates a hybrid attention module to enhance the extraction of spatial details. The effectiveness of PDHAM was evaluated using in situ observations across mainland China. PDHAM consistently outperformed a backpropagation neural network, a deep belief network, and a residual dense network, achieving an average correlation coefficient of 0.72 and an unbiased root-mean-square error of 0.061 m3/m3. Moreover, the downscaled results compared favorably with two existing high-resolution soil moisture datasets. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of PDHAM to improve fine-scale soil moisture monitoring and support hydrological, agricultural, and climatological applications.
item.authors: Peilong Chen;Yinghong Jing;Xiaojun She;Jiao Yang;Yao Li;

item.title: Turning Motion Offset From Liability to Asset: TSE-RD for GEO–LEO SAR Ship Localization
item.description: Reliable and high-precision localization of ships in remote ocean areas remains a critical yet challenging demand for maritime safety and global shipping management. The distributed configuration of geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (SAR) illuminator and low Earth orbit SAR receiver offers a promising architecture for persistent, wide-area maritime remote sensing. However, the accurate localization of moving ships remains challenging due to the inherent failure of the classical range–Doppler (RD) model, compounded by significant multisource observation errors. To address these issues, this article proposes a time-series-enhanced RD localization method. By establishing an offset transfer model across multiple frames to jointly estimate target position and velocity, it effectively overcomes the failure problem of the classical RD model. Furthermore, this article systematically models various error sources, including atmospheric delays, orbital determination errors, and time–frequency synchronization errors, and derives the Cramér–Rao lower bound for localization accuracy. Simulation results indicate that under the four-frame joint localization, the system achieves a tangential accuracy better than 500 m with a total synthetic aperture time of 10 s. Experimental validation based on airborne–ground bistatic SAR further demonstrates that the proposed method can attain a localization accuracy better than 60 m, significantly improving accuracy compared to traditional single-frame approaches.
item.authors: Jiayu Fu;Yuanhao Li;Feifeng Liu;Zhiyang Chen;Junhua Tian;Xiaodong Zang;Cheng Hu;

item.title: Physics-Guided Multitask Estimation of Tropical Cyclone Center, Intensity, and Radius of Maximum Wind From Geostationary Infrared Imagery
item.description: Tropical cyclone (TC) center location, intensity, and radius of maximum wind (RMW) are essential parameters for TC monitoring and hazard assessment. However, their joint estimation remains challenging because geostationary infrared (IR) cloud-top brightness temperature provides only indirect information on the near-surface vortex, particularly for weak, asymmetric, or poorly organized storms. This study presents physics-guided TC monitoring (PGTCM) model, a physics-guided, prior-conditioned multitask framework that estimates the current TC state from a current off-center GridSat-B1 IR image together with historical TC center, intensity, and RMW states from 6 and 12 h earlier. A point branch provides the final estimates, while an auxiliary map branch supplies label-derived spatial regularization. Vortex-profile-based auxiliary targets generated from Rankine, Holland, and Willoughby radial profiles encode center location, intensity-related response magnitude, and RMW-related radial scale, and a point-map consistency term links the two branches. Evaluation on independent 2023–2024 cases from the six major TC basins represented in the dataset yields a mean center-location error of 30.19 km, an intensity root-mean-square error of 2.35 m/s, and an RMW mean absolute error of 8.72 km. Ablation experiments show that the historical TC priors provide the largest performance improvement, while vortex-profile-based auxiliary maps provide additional gains in intensity and RMW estimation. The results support PGTCM as a retrospective prior-conditioned current-state estimation framework; real-time operational performance remains to be evaluated with operational first-guess inputs.
item.authors: Chong Wang;Shanshan Mu;Xiaofeng Li;

item.title: NSCAT5: A Geophysical Model Function for Space-Borne Ku-band Scatterometers, Including SST Dependence
item.description: This study investigates the incidence-angle dependence of sea surface temperature (SST) effects on Ku-band scatterometer normalized radar cross section (NRCS) and develops a generalized SST-dependent geophysical model function (GMF), referred to as NSCAT-5. Unlike previous SST-dependent Ku-band GMFs developed for individual fixed-incidence-angle scatterometers, NSCAT-5 extends the SST correction to a broader incidence-angle range for multimission Ku-band wind retrievals. Winds retrieved from the C-band scatterometer onboard the ERS-2 satellite (ESCAT) and onboard MetOp satellite (ASCAT), whose SST dependence is negligible compared with Ku-band winds, are used as SST-insensitive transfer references. Analysis of collocated ESCAT–NSCAT data and physics-based radar backscatter simulations shows that SST effects on Ku-band NRCS increase approximately linearly with incidence angle and become weak at low incidence angles. Reference SST correction coefficients are derived from closely collocated ASCAT and HY-2C scatterometer data and generalized through incidence-angle interpolation. Validation with NSCAT, RapidScat, ScatSat-1, HY-2 HY-2 series scatterometers, and WindRAD demonstrates that NSCAT-5 substantially reduces systematic SST-dependent wind speed biases, with the maximum SST-induced bias over the 0 °C–30 °C SST range reduced from more than 1.3 m/s to below 0.2 m/s. These results improve the consistency of multimission Ku- and C-band scatterometer winds and support integrated ocean surface wind applications.
item.authors: Zhixiong Wang;Juhong Zou;Qian Feng;Ad Stoffelen;Xiao-Ming Li;Anton Verhoef;Huimin Li;

item.title: Open-Set Domain Generalization via Spectral–Spatial Uncertainty Disentanglement for Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Open-set domain generalization (OSDG) aims to classify known samples and reject previously unseen classes in a target domain that is unavailable during training. For hyperspectral images, acquisition changes and novel materials can alter the same spectral measurements, making the two effects difficult to distinguish. An OSDG framework with separate spectral and spatial pathways whose uncertainties are estimated by evidential deep learning is proposed. The proposed spectral–spatial uncertainty disentanglement mechanism combines these estimates according to their samplewise reliability. The lower uncertainty pathway determines the base estimate, while a reduced contribution from the other pathway is intended to preserve complementary evidence of novelty. Spectrum-invariant frequency disentanglement is used to reduce acquisition-dependent spectral variation, and a dual-channel residual network maintains separate spectral and spatial representations before fusion. Across the Pavia University (PU)–Pavia Center (PC), Houston 2013–Houston 2018, and Dioni–Loukia benchmarks, the best HOS on PU–PC and the second-best HOS on the other two tasks are achieved by the proposed method, although unlabeled target data are used during training by the competing open-set domain adaptation methods.
item.authors: Amirreza Khoshbakht;Erchan Aptoula;

item.title: FDBGF-Net: Frequency-Decoupled Bidirectional Gated Fusion for Infrared–Visible Object Detection Under Degradation in UAV Imagery
item.description: Infrared–visible fusion is increasingly used to improve object detection robustness in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. However, real-world UAV imagery is often affected by co-occurring degradations, such as blur, rain, snow, fog, strong illumination, and electromagnetic interference. These disturbances may simultaneously corrupt both modalities, weaken cross-modal complementarity, and make conventional fusion schemes unreliable. To address this problem, we propose FDBGF-Net, a frequency-decoupled bidirectional gated fusion network for infrared–visible object detection under compound degradation. The proposed framework introduces three coordinated components. First, a dual-modal gated fusion network performs P3-level cross-modal alignment through selective state-space modeling, preserving geometric details before high-level semantic compression. Second, a degradation-aware gated fusion network employs a bidirectional gated feature pyramid and a spatial adaptive router to dynamically aggregate multiscale features according to modality reliability. Third, a Wavelet-Decoupled Frequency Attention module separates fused representations into low-frequency structural and high-frequency detail components, and adaptively recalibrates their contributions using dual-path channel gating. We also construct a benchmark containing 3711 infrared–visible image pairs, five target categories, six degradation types, and three severity levels. Experimental results show that FDBGF-Net achieves 79.8% mAP$_{50}$ on the proposed benchmark, outperforming DPAL-R by 1.5 percentage points at 76.3 FPS. It also reaches 79.6% mAP$_{50}$ on VEDAI and 88.1% mAP$_{50}$ on aligned FLIR after independent target-dataset retraining, demonstrating consistent cross-dataset applicability across substantially different data distributions.
item.authors: Kaipeng Wang;Guanglin He;Zongze Li;Xiaoyan Zheng;Hao Zhang;

item.title: JASTFR-Net: Joint Attention-Based Spatio-Temporal Feature Reconstruction Network for Multiframe Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Infrared small target detection plays a crucial role in a variety of remote sensing-related applications, such as maritime rescue, forest fire prevention, and precision guidance. However, the small size and weak intensity of infrared small targets, coupled with complex background clutter, make discriminative feature extraction difficult. Recent single-frame methods have substantially improved spatial feature learning for infrared small target detection. Nevertheless, methods based on an individual frame may remain vulnerable to target-like clutter and low-contrast backgrounds because they cannot exploit interframe consistency. Therefore, in this article, we propose a joint attention-based spatio-temporal feature reconstruction network, called JASTFR-Net, for multiframe infrared small target detection. First, a convolutional long short-term memory module based on a joint attention mechanism (JAconvLSTM) is fully exploited. By incorporating a joint attention mechanism into a temporal long short-term memory, the ability of detection network to extract spatial features of small targets is enhanced. Then, we design an edge-refined spatio-temporal feature reconstruction module for the purpose of enhancing spatio-temporal representation and accurate infrared small target segmentation in complex backgrounds. Specifically, a 3-D encoder module encodes the spatio-temporal feature map output by the JAconvLSTM module, extracting multiscale feature information layer by layer. Temporal weighted aggregation learns normalized weights for the relative frame positions and uses them to fuse the temporal features, after which a 2-D decoder restores the spatial locations and details. Besides, edge gradient information is introduced to optimize the feature reconstruction results, which further improves the ability to restore small target details. Experimental results show that our presented JASTFR-Net improves the intersection over union and $F_{1}$-measure scores by 5.34% and 3.30%, and 3.48% and 2.98% on the public NUDT-MIRSDT and TSIRMT datasets compared to the suboptimal method.
item.authors: Minjie Wan;Fubin Chu;Xiaofang Kong;Weixian Qian;Guohua Gu;Qian Chen;

item.title: SpectralDualIGANet: A Spectral-Prior-Guided Dual-Gated Segmentation Network for Fine-Grained Segmentation of Aquatic Invasive Plants
item.description: Floating aquatic invasive plants, represented by water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), can rapidly form extensive surface coverage in inland water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs, leading to substantial ecological and economic losses. Therefore, efficient, fine-grained, and continuous dynamic monitoring is urgently needed. uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides high-resolution observations for such surveys. However, in complex aquatic environments, aquatic invasive plants are prone to spectral and textural confusion with riparian vegetation, water shadows, and surrounding backgrounds. Moreover, slight spatial misalignment between RGB and multispectral imagery may further weaken the effectiveness of cross-modal feature fusion. To address these challenges, this study proposes SpectralDualIGANet, a spectral-prior-guided dual-gated segmentation network for fine-grained segmentation of aquatic invasive plants. The proposed method employs a learnable spectral alignment module to compensate for cross-modal spatial offsets and transforms physically meaningful spectral indices, including NDVI, NDRE, and NDWI, into learnable priors. These priors are then used to guide feature modulation through a dual-gating mechanism, thereby enhancing target responses while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms mainstream unimodal and multimodal approaches under random split testing and maintains stable performance in a within-lake cross-region transfer test between two spatially separated subregions of the same lake system. Specifically, under complex background conditions, the proposed method achieves an IoU of 94.66% and a Dice coefficient of 97.25% for water hyacinth segmentation, while maintaining an IoU above 91% in within-lake cross-region testing. Overall, the proposed method provides reliable technical support for coverage estimation and dynamic monitoring of aquatic invasive plants.
item.authors: Xiaomei Yi;Jie Wang;Lufeng Mo;Guoying Wang;Peng Wu;

item.title: An Integrated Spatial–Temporal Framework for Annual Forest Canopy Height Mapping Using Fused GEDI and ICESat-2 Data
item.description: Forest canopy height (FCH) is essential for characterizing forest vertical structure and supporting biomass, carbon-stock, and ecosystem assessments. This study developed a framework for annual FCH mapping in Heilongjiang Province, China, from 2020 to 2024 by integrating consistency-corrected GEDI and ICESat-2/ATL08 observations with optical, synthetic aperture radar, topographic, and climatic variables. A multiscale attention convolutional neural network with center feature fusion (MSA-CNN-CF) was first used for spatially continuous FCH retrieval, followed by graph-based residual diffusion (Graph-RD) to reduce spatially structured errors. Compared with a conventional CNN, MSA-CNN-CF increased the average $R^{2}$ from 0.54 to 0.61 and reduced RMSE from 5.07 to 4.20 m. Graph-RD further increased the average $R^{2}$ to 0.70 and reduced RMSE to 3.58 m. An adaptive spatio-temporal trend constraint (ASTC) method was then used to retrospectively reconstruct the missing 2023 FCH map. In a simulated missing-year experiment, ASTC achieved an $R^{2}$ of 0.92 and an RMSE of 1.52 m in stable undisturbed forests. In forests disturbed in 2022, ASTC achieved an RMSE of 3.62 m, representing a 47.96% reduction relative to linear interpolation. The proposed framework improves the spatial continuity and temporal completeness of regional FCH products and provides a practical basis for forest structural monitoring and carbon assessment.
item.authors: Guanran Wang;Ying Yu;Xiguang Yang;Hanyuan Dong;Xuebing Guan;Hang Xu;

item.title: Expert-Instruction and Quality-Assessment Guided Refinement of Binary Geo-Entity Masks via Latent Rectified Flow
item.description: Automatic extraction of binary geo-entity masks from remote sensing imagery is fundamental to a wide range of geo-spatial tasks. Nevertheless, even advanced segmentation networks frequently produce outputs marred by boundary irregularities, merging of adjacent instances, and structural fragmentation. Typical mask optimization approaches are often constrained: hand-crafted algorithms suffer from limited transferability across scenes, while learning-based methods are usually embedded within specific architectures, hindering their reusability. To bridge this gap, we introduce OptimFlow, a decoupled refinement framework that reformulates mask optimization as a multicondition image editing task. Built upon a latent rectified flow architecture, OptimFlow synergizes two complementary conditions to guide the refinement process: category-level expert instructions in natural language that offer global semantic priors over the optimization process, and a panoramic quality assessment map that provides pixelwise spatial guidance by pinpointing correct and erroneous regions. Furthermore, we introduce a confidence-based voting strategy to suppress the granular noise often produced by generative models on low-entropy binary masks. Extensive experiments across building, water, and road datasets demonstrate that OptimFlow consistently improves both mask-level and geometry-level accuracy over various segmentation models. These results indicate that our approach can serve as a flexible postprocessing solution for binary mask refinement.
item.authors: Bingnan Yang;Mingjun Peng;Zhan Zhang;Jianya Gong;Mi Zhang;

item.title: SARES-DEIM: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Meets DETR for Clutter-Aware SAR Ship Detection
item.description: Ship detectionin synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is challenged by coherent speckle noise, complex coastal clutter, and the prevalence of small-scale targets. Conventional detectors, primarily designed for optical imagery, often exhibit limited adaptability to SAR-specific degradation and suffer from the loss of fine-grained ship signatures during spatial downsampling. To address these limitations, we propose SARES-DEIM, a domain-aware detection framework grounded in the detection transformer (DETR) paradigm. Central to our approach is SAR-aware expert selection mixture-of-experts (SARESMoE), a module leveraging a sparse gating mechanism to selectively route features toward specialized wavelet, spatial, and frequency-oriented experts. This sparsely activated architecture enhances clutter-aware representation while keeping the active inference cost controlled. Furthermore, we introduce the space-to-depth enhancement pyramid (SDEP) neck to preserve high-resolution spatial cues from shallow stages and improve the localization of small targets. Experiments on HRSID and SAR-Ship-Dataset show that SARES-DEIM achieves competitive results across both public benchmarks, with more prominent advantages on the challenging HRSID dataset. Specifically, SARES-DEIM achieves 76.4% $mAP_{50:95}$ and 93.8% $mAP_{50}$ on HRSID, while keeping the active computation at 72.6 GFLOPs and 136.5 FPS on a single NVIDIA A40 GPU with batch size 8; the batch-size-1 latency is 37.6 ms.
item.authors: Fenghao Song;Shaojing Yang;Xi Zhou;

item.title: Jacobian-Based Identifiability Diagnostics for Multispectral CDOM Retrieval in Optically Complex Inland Waters
item.description: Retrieving the absorption coefficient of chromophoric dissolved organic matter at 440 nm from seven multispectral reflectance bands can be weakly constrained. We combine fixed-coefficient Gordon-model diagnostics with retrieval experiments on 2682 quality-controlled in situ spectra. The normalized-coordinate, noise-whitened reference Jacobians concentrated 99.63% of cohort sensitivity energy in two singular modes within the bounded nonlinear-least-squares state domain; these model-conditional diagnostics do not establish global uniqueness. Conditioning deteriorated below 0.2 m$^{-\text{1}}$, where absorption–backscattering-exponent coupling strengthened without becoming the dominant global pair. The evaluated retrieval model uses seven reflectance inputs and a six-component soft optical-type branch that learns its optical coefficients. Across five repeated lake-level holdouts, its mean root-mean-square error was 0.398 in base-10 logarithmic units, with a mean coefficient of determination of 0.385. Against a protocol-matched mixture density network, the paired lake-cluster bootstrap difference in that error was $-\text{0.0076}$ (95% interval $[-\text{0.0286}, +\text{0.0154}]$), so no global advantage is claimed. Condition-number regularization was evaluated and excluded; auxiliary chlorophyll supervision improved chlorophyll prediction but did not establish noninferiority for the target variable. The lowest observed-concentration bin remained a benchmark-specific low-confidence regime. A reflectance-domain transfer test on 27 Sentinel-2B match-ups gave a descriptive error difference of $-\text{0.105}$, but both models were strongly biased and the corresponding in situ records overlapped development partitions; no satellite-level superiority or independent generalization claim is made.
item.authors: Chuishun Kong;Jiayi Ma;Fan Fan;Xiaoguang Mei;Yong Ma;

item.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Identification Dominant Species in Harmful Algal Blooms Using Broadband Satellite Data
item.description: Harmful algal blooms (HABs), are worldwide marine ecological disasters marked by diverse dominant species. Identifying these species is critical due to their differing ecological impacts and toxicity. The broadband optical satellites offer advantages for monitoring fine-scale nearshore HABs. However, most of them have low spectral resolution and few bands, which poses a significant challenge to accurate species identification. To address these issues, this study developed a deep learning-based framework for identifying HABs dominant species (RT-SGINet). The framework integrates a spectral feature transfer-based sample generation strategy to produce high-quality 3-D red tide samples, alleviating the uneven distribution of species-specific training data. The dominant species identification module based on cross-spatial feature fusion was developed to enhance interspecies separability by jointly extracting spectral and spatial-structural features. Furthermore, a student–teacher semisupervised learning strategy was introduced to improve generalizability across different species distributions. The experimental results demonstrated that the sample generation module preserves high spatial-spectral fidelity, enabling precise species identification in few-shot scenarios. RT–SGINet accurately identifies three dominant species, including Akashiwo sanguinea in the East China Sea, red Noctiluca scintillans, and green Noctiluca scintillans, with an overall accuracy of 94.5%. Compared with existing methods, RT-SGINet significantly improves the identification accuracy by 3.52%–8.66%. The model exhibited strong generalization capabilities across various areas and broadband satellite sensors. This study provides a generalizable deep learning framework for fine-grained HAB species identification under spectrally limited and sample-imbalanced conditions.
item.authors: Xin Zhao;Yanfang Xiao;Yi Ma;Yujie Chen;Wei Zhao;Na Liu;Baohua Shan;Manli Zhou;Rongjie Liu;

item.title: Small Object Detection in Multimodal Remote Sensing via Shared-Differential Modality Collaborative Interaction Fusion
item.description: To address the insufficient fusion of shared and complementary features between modalities in infrared-visible small object detection, this study proposes a method named CIFYOLO, which integrates cross-modality global feature interaction and fusion with local feature's super-resolution reconstruction. We design a novel collaborative interaction fusion module of shared-differential mode (SDCIF) based on shared-guided fusion enhancement and complementary-guided fusion regulation. This module is capable of extracting both the consistent and distinctive features of infrared and visible modalities while enabling mutual regulation between them. By avoiding the redundancies and conflicts caused by separate processing, it enhances cross-modal collaborative representations and improves the perception and discrimination of weak-texture targets. In addition, to further enhance the model's structural perception ability for small object regions, a local perception enhanced super-resolution (LPE-SR) branch is leveraged. By applying convolutional kernels of different sizes to focus on detailed features at different scales of local regions, the discriminability and robustness of the model for remote sensing small objects can be improved. In this study, the term “object recognition” refers specifically to the object detection task, including target localization and category prediction, rather than image-level classification. Experimental results show that CIFYOLO achieves 77.1% mAP on the vehicle detection in aerial imagery (VEDAI) dataset, performing better than the baseline model and several mainstream methods.
item.authors: Guoqiang Zhou;Weiting Huang;Yating Liu;Qian Liu;Aiai Ren;Xu Zhou;Haoran Li;Zeyu Huang;Weifeng Zhang;Jun Shen;

item.title: SSPNet: Spatial-Semantic Foundation Prior Network for Remote Sensing Few-Shot Segmentation
item.description: Few-shot segmentation seeks to identify and delineate target objects in a query image with the guidance of only a handful of annotated support samples. While considerable progress has been made on natural image benchmarks, applying these techniques to remote sensing imagery remains challenging due to the pronounced intraclass appearance diversity and the pervasive spectral confusion between foreground and background. In this article, we propose a spatial-semantic foundation prior network (SSPNet) that harnesses two heterogeneous frozen foundation models to address these difficulties. SSPNet comprises a dual-stream multimodal semantic fusion (DMSF) module and a dynamic class activation map (CAM)-guided mask-aware cross-attention (DCMA) module. The DMSF module employs a frozen DINOv2 encoder and a frozen GeoRSCLIP text encoder whose representations originate from different pretraining objectives; a learnable cross-modal projection maps the language representation into the spatial feature space, enabling complementary spatial and semantic CAMs to be constructed in a shared hidden space. The DCMA module then incorporates the fused activation prior through bounded residual modulation and foreground-constrained cross-attention. An auxiliary pseudomask objective provides a downstream-to-prior gradient pathway through the learnable activation-generation and feature-refinement layers, coupling their optimization during episodic training. Experiments on the iSAID-5$^{i}$ and LoveDA-2$^{i}$ benchmarks show that SSPNet achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across the evaluated settings, with the most pronounced improvements under the one-shot protocol.
item.authors: Yi Zhong;Guodong Zhao;

item.title: Multifrequency Microwave Signatures of Layered Soil Moisture and Temperature Profile Variations Using an NMM3D-VIE-DDA Model
item.description: This study investigates how depth-dependent variations in soil moisture and temperature affect active and passive microwave simulated observables using a full-wave NMM3D-VIE-DDA model. Baseline profiles are constructed from in situ measurements in Saihanba (Hebei, China), and profile scenarios are generated to represent variations concentrated in the shallow (0 cm), middle (3 cm), and deep (5 cm) layers, together with piecewise-constant approximations. Simulations are performed at 1.26 and 6.925 GHz for incidence angles of $30^\circ$, $40^\circ$, and $50^\circ$, with convergence at 6.925 GHz assessed using $n_{r} = 15$ Monte Carlo realizations of statistically generated rough surfaces. Across the tested cases, profile scenarios with shallow-layer variations produce the largest changes in backscattering, interferometric phase, and brightness temperature, whereas scenarios with middle- and deep-layer variations have weaker effects. A key contribution is the interferometric analysis: phase separability is stronger at 1.26 GHz than at 6.925 GHz, with coherence remaining high ($>0.99$), supporting stable phase interpretation. Meanwhile, the coherence with respect to soil moisture variations exhibits a roughness and frequency dependent pattern. For passive simulated observations, polarization and frequency jointly control sensitivity: V/H brightness-temperature contrast increases with observation angle from 30$^{\circ }$ to 50$^{\circ }$, and the strongest correlation with the simulated brightness temperature shifts from the 0–20 cm mean soil temperature at 1.26 GHz to the 0–3 cm mean soil temperature at 6.925 GHz. A practically important result is that piecewise-constant profiles at 1 cm resolution interval and continuous profiles produce closely matched responses in both active and passive channels under the tested setup, supporting simplified layered parameterization for retrieval-oriented modeling within a validated domain. The results provide bounded, physically consistent guidance for multichannel retrieval algorithm design, and the main qualitative conclusions remain valid under several additional reference roughness conditions considered in this study.
item.authors: Shaojie Xu;Jiancheng Shi;Shurun Tan;

item.title: Physics-Guided Interpretable SAR Image Generation: Bridging Simulation and Reality With Explicit Geometric and Statistical Modeling
item.description: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image interpretation is limited by the scarcity of labeled measured data, especially for specific vehicle targets and observation conditions. Physics-based simulation can provide target geometry and scattering locations, but the resulting images usually lack the blur, clutter, and speckle statistics observed in measured SAR data. To address this gap, we propose PI-SAR-Net, a SAR image generation method that combines geometric simulation with a learnable rendering stage. Starting from a 3-D target model and SAR sensor parameters, an equivalent-beam-integration simulator first produces a geometry-guided SAR image. A generator then aligns the simulated image, predicts a pixelwise reflectivity map, and renders the final image with realistic blur, clutter, and speckle statistics. The observation condition vector encodes azimuth, incidence angle, and polarization, while a multitask style encoder estimates the style, speckle strength, and blur strength required for rendering from measured reference images. We construct a paired vehicle SAR dataset with simulated and measured images under matched observation conditions. Experiments show that PI-SAR-Net improves paired image fidelity, SAR-specific background statistics, and few-shot real-SAR recognition performance compared with simulation-only and image-translation baselines.
item.authors: Hao Ye;Guowang Jin;Xin Xiong;Hongmin Zhang;Jiahao Li;Miao Xu;

item.title: A Physical Prior-Informed Framework for Joint Detection and Suppression of Radio Frequency Interference in SAR Amplitude Images
item.description: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems have been increasingly subjected to severe radio frequency interference (RFI), which has led to significant degradation in imaging quality and hindered the effective utilization of ground range detected products. However, existing deep learning-based RFI suppression methods often suffer from the loss of texture detail information, insufficient preservation of salient targets, and limited physical interpretability. To address these issues, we first establish the signal and image model for diverse RFI patterns in the image domain. Based on this, we propose PPRNet, a physical prior-informed framework for joint detection and suppression. Specifically, an adaptive subspace projection layer is developed to physically isolate blanket jamming by exploiting the low-rank singular value characteristics of the interference subspace. Concurrently, a shallow jamming detector is designed to precisely localize interference regions through statistical power anomaly detection across multiple spatial dimensions. A multistage progressive target reconstruction subnetwork then integrates these physical priors to recover obscured terrain textures. Experiments on Sentinel-1 and airborne platforms validate the effectiveness of PPRNet, yielding a 14.51 dB peak signal to noise ratio improvement in specific interference scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework exhibits superior performance in suppressing various RFI types, thereby achieving high-quality, interference-free SAR imagery.
item.authors: Lin Nie;Dongfang Guan;Keli Huang;Shuowei Liu;Zhen Liu;Yong-xiang Liu;

item.title: Multiscale Characterization and Attribution of Earth's Oblateness Variations Using an SVMD–SSA Approach
item.description: Earth's oblateness variation (ΔJ2) is a key indicator of global-scale mass redistribution and Earth system dynamics. However, the coexistence of long-term, seasonal, interannual, and decadal signals, together with strong noise contamination and signal mixing, poses significant challenges for accurately characterizing its multiscale variability. Singular spectrum analysis (SSA) may have difficulty separating different temporal-scale components with comparable variance contributions, whereas successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD) is susceptible to noise-dominated modes and mode mixing. To overcome these limitations, an SVMD–SSA-based signal analysis approach integrating SVMD and SSA is proposed. Multisource satellite-derived geodetic datasets spanning 1976–2024, including satellite laser ranging observations and gravity recovery and climate experiment (GRACE)-derived gravity field solutions, are employed for multiscale analysis and geophysical attribution. Compared with empirical mode decomposition and discrete wavelet transform, SVMD provides clearer separation and reconstruction of the long-term, seasonal, interannual, and decadal components of ΔJ2, while SSA further identifies the dominant periodic signals within these temporal scales. The extracted long-term component reveals the transition of ΔJ2 from a steady decrease to a slowdown and subsequent reversal after 2002. Seasonal variability is dominated by terrestrial water storage, atmospheric pressure, and ocean mass redistribution, whereas interannual fluctuations exhibit strong associations with major climate modes, including El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Arctic Oscillation, Antarctic Oscillation, and Pacific Decadal Oscillation. Decadal variability further suggests potential links with solar activity and ENSO-related teleconnections. The proposed approach provides an effective tool for characterizing multiscale gravity-field variability and facilitates the investigation of Earth system mass redistribution using satellite geodetic observations.
item.authors: Hongjuan Yu;Penglong Zhang;Yu Sun;Krzysztof Sośnica;Yong Zhang;

item.title: Learning to Guide: An Adaptive Multisource Prompting and Geometric-Semantic Refinement Network for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
item.description: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images faces multiple challenges, including complex spatial structures, high intraclass variability, and insufficient cross-modal registration accuracy. Although foundation models, such as Segment Anything Model (SAM), exhibit strong generalizability, their direct application to remote sensing tasks is limited by their reliance on manual prompts and insufficient adaptation to domain-specific characteristics. To overcome these challenges, we propose an adaptive multisource prompting and geometric-semantic refinement network (MPGNet), which addresses complex spatial structures in remote sensing images through multidimensional guided reoptimization. First, we introduce a parameter-efficient adapter that integrates low-rank adaptation and snake-like linear layers into the SAM backbone to meticulously extract fine-grained textures and long-range dependencies from the RGB modality. Second, to handle complex topological variations, we design a dual-branch filtering module (using CNN and Transformer pathways) for the normalized digital surface model (nDSM). This module adaptively evaluates and selects the most reliable feature pathway and generates point and bounding box prompts without manual intervention. Third, RGB and nDSM features are synergistically fused through two complementary pathways: polygon boundary prompts for geometric structure refinement, and contrastive language-image pretraining text embeddings for robust semantic alignment. Finally, a hierarchical decoder integrates the aligned multimodal features with the generated spatial and semantic prompts to produce the final segmentation results. Extensive experiments on the Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets demonstrate that MPGNet outperforms various existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of mean accuracy and mean intersection over union, highlighting the superiority of combining multimodal automatic prompting with cross-modal geometric refinement.
item.authors: Shenghao Qi;Weiwei Qiu;Liang Liao;Yuanyuan Liu;Wujie Zhou;

item.title: A Pseudo-Random Coded Ground-Penetrating Radar for Glacier Thickness Detection
item.description: Accurately detecting and evaluating glacier thickness and ice reserves is of great significance for global climate change research and ecological environment protection of high frigid regions. A pseudorandom coded radar mounted on an uncrewed vehicle is developed to measure the subglacial topography and glacier thickness with high accuracy. Using the Golay complementary code as the transmitted signal and operating at the frequency range of 10–130 MHz with code length of 1024 bits, this radar system offers a range resolution of about 1.5 m in ice. The interleaved sampling of deep detection mode and shallow detection mode is used to improve the detection dynamic range of the system. In order to reduce the detection blind zone of deep mode, the pseudorandom encoded long pulse signal is divided into short pulses for transmission and reception, and the shift superposition is completed in the real-time processor to reduce the data rate of the radar. An IO pin of field programmable gate array is used to generate a pseudorandom encoded signal modulated by square carrier in series, which serves as the input source for the transmitter. A radio frequency switch in the receiving path is applied to prevent saturation of the receiver front-end and collect radar loop data as a reference signal for pulse compression. In addition, a frequency wavenumber domain migration algorithm is proposed to obtain a high processing gain and to improve the signal to noise ratio of the system. Field experiments at Bayi Glacier in northwestern China demonstrate clear imaging of ice-bedrock interfaces, while link-budget analysis suggests a potential detection capability of up to approximately 400 m under comparable ice-loss conditions.
item.authors: Bo Zhao;Yan Liu;Shidong Li;Xiaojun Liu;Guangyou Fang;

item.title: Lightweight Remote-Sensing Image Super- Resolution via Uncertainty-Guided Contextual Token Aggregation Network
item.description: Recent advances in remote sensing image super-resolution (RSISR) have achieved remarkable progress. However, restoring fine structural details in complex scenes and efficiently modeling spatial heterogeneity remain challenging. In addition, many existing methods rely on computationally expensive dense global interactions, which limits their practical applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. To address these issues, we propose an Uncertainty-Guided Contextual Token Aggregation Network (UCTAN) for RSISR. The proposed network consists of two key designs. First, a Contextualized Aggregation Block (CAB) is introduced to cluster spatial tokens into compact contextual representations, enabling efficient and stable contextual token aggregation. This design reduces redundant computation while enhancing the modeling of local details and global structures. Second, an Uncertainty-Guided Token Interaction module is developed to exploit local uncertainty information estimated from feature variance, which complementarily guides contextual interaction and spatial refinement, thereby improving the adaptive modeling capability of the network for complex regions and high-frequency details. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UCTAN achieves superior or competitive performance on multiple remote sensing datasets and attains a favorable balance between reconstruction quality and computational complexity, validating its effectiveness and practical value for real-world RSISR tasks.
item.authors: Yongxin Liu;Shuli Cheng;Liejun Wang;Yikemaiti Sataer;

item.title: Explainable CyGNSSnet: Deep-Learning Retrieval of Global GNSS-R Soil Moisture
item.description: Global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) enables high-revisit soil moisture (SM) monitoring, but retrieval over land remains confounded by vegetation, roughness, and topography. We present explainable CyGNSSnet, a hybrid deep-learning retrieval that fuses the full Cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) delay-Doppler maps (DDMs) and derived observables with daily moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer optical/thermal indices and static topographic, biomass, and eco-climatic descriptors. The model is trained on 2019–2020 data, with soil moisture active passive (SMAP) L3 soil moisture as the reference, and tested on the fully independent year 2021 and against International Soil Moisture Network (ISMN) stations. CyGNSSnet reaches a correlation coefficient $R=0.90$ and a root mean square error $\text{RMSE}=0.046\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$ on the 2021 test set. In addition, a SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) audit shows a physically consistent retrieval: the GNSS-R amplitude metrics provide the sensitivity to the soil dielectric properties, and hence, to soil moisture; vegetation indices and biomass carry the vegetation conditioning; and DDM attributions concentrate near the quasi-specular core. Relative to an auxiliary-only model with no CYGNSS input, the GNSS-R observables remove 25% of the error variance and raise the per-cell temporal correlation from 0.35 to 0.51: they mainly supply the temporal (wetting–drying) signal of soil moisture, while the auxiliaries reproduce the time-mean spatial pattern. Triple collocation at the ISMN stations bounds the SM random error at the SMAP level ($\sim 0.03\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$, a lower bound because CyGNSSnet is trained on SMAP). A SMAP-enhanced control that adds SMAP-derived vegetation water content and optical depth, as often done in the literature, improves RMSE by only $0.004\,\mathrm{m^{3}\,m^{-3}}$, yet SHAP shows these inputs dominating its attribution, a fingerprint of input–target coupling that justifies their exclusion. Requiring no SMAP-derived input at inference time, Explainable CyGNSSnet can be retrained on other GNSS-R missions, such as HydroGNSS and support soil-moisture monitoring beyond the SMAP era.
item.authors: Hamed Izadgoshasb;Luke J. Pugin;Tianqi Xiao;Nazzareno Pierdicca;Jens Wickert;Milad Asgarimehr;

item.title: Physics-Driven Latent Diffusion Model for Multispectral Satellite Image Forecasting
item.description: Temporal gaps in multispectral satellite acquisitions, caused by orbital revisit constraints and atmospheric influence, limit the applicability of Earth Observation data for continuous environmental monitoring. Diffusion probabilistic models offer a compelling generative framework for multispectral image forecasting, owing to their ability to model complex high-dimensional distributions while preserving spatial structure and cross-band correlations. Conditioning such models on physical atmospheric and meteorological variables can further guide the prediction of environmental dynamics, improving forecast reliability and the agreement of the generated imagery with the observed environmental conditions. To address this, we propose a physics-guided latent diffusion framework that implements a dual forecasting strategy: first, a Mamba state-space model predicts future physical drivers from historical observations, then the predicted physical variables condition a latent diffusion module to synthesize the corresponding multispectral imagery. This work provides a comprehensive experimental evaluation of the proposed model, including ablation studies on key hyperparameters and additional quantitative metrics. We validate the proposed model on 13-band Copernicus Sentinel-2 time series in a water-body dynamics monitoring scenario, with direct relevance to drought assessment and environmental risk management. The results show that physics-guided conditioning generally improves the latent diffusion-based forecasting framework, particularly in terms of structural and spatial consistency, while the relative performance with respect to alternative forecasting architectures may vary in more challenging out-of-distribution scenarios. Moreover, the performance gap between predicted and exact conditioning variables remains limited.
item.authors: Francesca De Falco;Francesco Mauro;Andrea Ceschini;Alessandro Sebastianelli;Paolo Gamba;Silvia Ullo;Gabriele Meoni;Massimo Panella;Lorenzo Papa;

item.title: DviCD: Lightweight Multiscale Calibration for High-Resolution Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify land-cover changes from bitemporal images while suppressing pseudo changes caused by illumination variations, seasonal differences, and viewpoint shifts. However, lightweight RSCD models still face challenges in multiscale feature interaction and boundary preservation. To address these issues, we propose DviCD, a lightweight Siamese network based on HRNetW18 with a hierarchical multiscale calibration framework. The network maintains high-resolution representations throughout feature extraction and introduces progressive feature calibration to enhance semantic guidance for shallow features. Specifically, a dual variation alignment (DVA) module is designed to model bitemporal feature inconsistencies from a dual-branch perspective. It decomposes bitemporal discrepancies into complementary change and consistency representations, followed by adaptive alignment to suppress unreliable variations while preserving discriminative change cues. Furthermore, a cross-scale (DVA) module is introduced to perform cross-scale feature calibration, enabling effective integration of local structural details and high-level semantic context. To further improve spatial precision, a lightweight details injection module is employed to recover boundary information lost during feature aggregation and enhance fine-grained structural awareness. Extensive experiments on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method. DviCD achieves 85.60% Intersection over Union and 92.24% F1-score on LEVIR-CD with only 18.49M parameters and 15.63 GFLOPs, achieving a favorable tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency.
item.authors: Guangping Li;Zhenxuan He;Jing Ling;Di Dong;

item.title: Mapping Boreal Forest Canopy Height in Northeast China by Synergistic Use of LT-1 InSAR and GEDI LiDAR Data
item.description: China's L-band LuTan-1 (LT-1) satellite constellation can acquire single-pass bistatic interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) data with an appropriate spatial baseline, effectively avoiding temporal decorrelation while providing the vertical sensitivity associated with forest volume decorrelation. However, its routine single-baseline and single-polarization observation configuration could render forest canopy height inversion underdetermined by using traditional coherent scattering models. Aiming at this problem, we here propose a new method of forest canopy height retrieval from bistatic LT-1 InSAR data based on a simplified volume decorrelation model constrained by global ecosystem dynamics investigation (GEDI) LiDAR observations. Instead of adopting fixed empirical parameters, spatiotemporally matched GEDI RH98 canopy height samples were used to separately calibrate the vertical scattering scale parameter and coherence correction parameter for four LT-1 interferometric pairs over the boreal forests of the Greater Khingan Mountains. The results show that the relationship between LT-1 coherence magnitude and the product of vertical wavenumber and GEDI forest height can be well described by the C-SINC model, yielding R2 values ranging from 0.435 to 0.569. The obtained canopy height mosaic agrees well with airborne LiDAR reference values, with an RMSE of 3.89 m and a bias of 1.30 m, outperforming the Meta CHMv2 product with an RMSE of 5.48 m and a bias of −4.30 m.
item.authors: Pengyuan Tan;Lu Zhang;Jiali Hou;Carlos López-Martínez;Peng Shen;Chuanjun Wu;Mingsheng Liao;

item.title: Ocean Front Prediction With a Spatiotemporal Hybrid Deep Network
item.description: Accurate prediction of ocean front evolution is critical for climate research, marine ecosystem management, and underwater acoustic applications, yet remains exceptionally challenging due to the multiscale, nonlinear, and strongly coupled spatiotemporal dynamics inherent in mesoscale processes. This article investigates a domain-specific formulation for ocean front forecasting, namely structure-aware residual prediction of the SST-gradient field (Ocean Front Prediction Network, OFPNet). The formulation is implemented using established spatial, temporal, feature-fusion, and structural-loss components, whose roles are coordinated to test this hypothesis. A gated convolutional long short-term memory with dual memory states is designed to enhance the model‘s capacity for capturing information across multiple temporal scales, and a cross-attention-based fusion mechanism that adaptively integrates spatial and temporal representations. To overcome the limitations of conventional pixelwise loss functions in frontal zone characterization, a multicomponent loss strategy is introduced, combining gradient loss, frontal structure similarity loss, and total variation regularization to jointly optimize numerical accuracy, morphological fidelity, and edge sharpness. Extensive experiments conducted on Moving MNIST and two satellite-derived sea surface temperature datasets (OISST and JCOPE2M) demonstrate that OFPNet achieves highly competitive performance against competitive performance against the evaluated spatiotemporal baselines spatiotemporal prediction models. Specifically, OFPNet demonstrates clear advantages in numerical accuracy (RMSE, MAE) and global morphological fidelity (Hu Similarity), underscoring its superior capability to preserve the complex geometry. Notably, OFPNet achieves substantial improvements in structural similarity and Hu moment invariance metrics, underscoring its superior capability to preserve the complex geometry and continuity of thermal fronts over forecasting horizons up to seven days. While true ocean front dynamics are governed by multiphysics processes, and the current results do not yet demonstrate a physically consistent ocean front forecasting system, the proposed framework offers a robust, structurally-aware, data-driven approach for forecasting the kinematic evolution of sea surface temperature fronts. It is important to clarify that OFPNet directly predicts the continuous SST gradient magnitude field (a gridded scalar field representing frontal intensity at each pixel) from which discrete frontal structures are subsequently extracted via a postprocessing pipeline. Our framework is, therefore, best characterized as gradient-field prediction with structure-aware optimization, rather than an explicit front-dynamics simulator that predicts the trajectories, births, and deaths of individual fronts. This distinction shapes both our methodological design and evaluation strategy.
item.authors: Xiang Wan;Lei Zhang;Maolin Li;Xiaodong Ma;Weishuai Xu;

item.title: FusionGaussian: Incremental 3-D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Aerial Photogrammetry
item.description: Large-scale unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry is essential for geospatial modeling, where 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) has recently shown transformative potential for high-fidelity reconstruction. However, existing 3DGS frameworks for large-scale scenes often rely on static partitioning and lack the flexibility needed for incremental expansion. When updating models with multimission data, these methods incur prohibitive computational costs for global retraining and exhibit geometric inconsistencies at fusion boundaries. To address these limitations, we propose FusionGaussian, a novel framework for scalable and incremental scene reconstruction based on 3DGS. Our approach enables independent training of subscenes captured from different UAV missions and supports incremental integration without global retraining. Specifically, we incorporate an overlap-aware view selection and boundary refinement strategy to address insufficient supervision in boundary regions, along with a blockwise competitive merging mechanism to improve rendering quality and geometric consistency during scene fusion. Extensive experiments on four real-world UAV datasets and two temporal update case studies demonstrate that FusionGaussian consistently outperforms direct-merge incremental baselines in rendering and geometric quality, particularly in overlapping regions, while achieving competitive full-scene quality and substantially lower cumulative reconstruction cost than repeated Global-All reconstruction.
item.authors: Zhenyu Xia;Pengcheng Han;Lin Chen;Boni Hu;Shuhui Bu;

item.title: Exploiting CNN and ViT Strengths: Local and Global Feature Fusion for Enhanced Remote Sensing Super-Resolution
item.description: The transmission and compression of remote sensing images often require reduced spatial resolution to improve bandwidth and storage efficiency, motivating the reconstruction of high-quality images from low-resolution inputs. To simulate this degradation, we generate low-resolution images using bicubic downsampling. Vision Transformers (ViTs) capture long-range dependencies for recovering global terrain structures, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) effectively preserve local textures and structural details. Accordingly, we propose a dual-stream architecture that integrates ViT and CNN features through a bidirectional feature fusion module, which alleviates the representation discrepancy between ViT patch features and convolutional feature maps. By jointly exploiting global context and local details, the proposed method enables coherent reconstruction of large-scale landscapes and fine-grained infrastructure. Extensive experiments on satellite image super-resolution datasets with different spatial resolutions demonstrate its effectiveness in recovering high-frequency details and preserving critical geospatial information.
item.authors: Chenghao Qiu;Aiping Ye;Cong Lin;Xu Cheng;

item.title: Adversarial Patch Attack on Ship Detection via Localized Data Augmentation
item.description: Current ship detection techniques based on remote sensing imagery primarily rely on the object detection capabilities of deep neural networks (DNNs). However, DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial patch attacks, which can deceive the detection model and lead to misclassifications. Numerous studies have demonstrated that data augmentation-based methods can improve the transferability of adversarial patches. However, excessive augmentation of image backgrounds or irrelevant regions may introduce unnecessary interference, which also resulting in false detections of the detection models. When using such kind of loss to optimize the adversarial patches, it will inevitably lead to the optimization direction deviating from correct track, because these loss are not caused by the adversarial patches themselves but rather by the overaugmentation of background and nontarget areas. Therefore, this article proposes a localized data augmentation method that applies augmentation only to the target regions, avoiding any influence on nontarget areas. By reducing background interference, this approach enables the loss function to focus more directly on the impact of the adversarial patches on the detection model, thereby improving the attack success rate. Experiments conducted on the HRSC2016 dataset have confirmed our hypotheses. When compared with the baselines, including the global data augmentation based method, the proposed method shows the ability to increase the attack success rate of adversarial patches and enhance their transferability across different object detection models.
item.authors: Chun Liu;Panpan Ding;Zheng Zheng;Hailong Wang;Bingqian Zhu;Tao Xu;Guangxia Wang;

item.title: QL-Sec: Quantum AI-Enabled Security Framework for LLM-Driven Low-Altitude Remote Sensing Networks
item.description: Low-altitude remote sensing network technology has advanced rapidly, especially with the assistance of large language models (LLMs). The use of LLMs, especially with autonomous aerial vehicles in remote sensing systems, poses significant security and privacy risks due to the need to transmit sensitive information and to enable large-scale distributed communication. This article introduces the quantum AI security (QL-Sec) framework for LLM-powered low-altitude remote sensing networks. The proposed solution utilizes a hybrid QL-Sec mechanism designed to enhance confidentiality, integrity, and authentication, and to resist adversarial intrusions. The framework also uses quantum-secured encryption and privacy-preserving feature perturbation to help reduce information leakage during edge–cloud communication. Results reveal that the proposed framework achieves 96.41% attack detection accuracy, a secret key rate of 0.91 bits/use, and a reduced quantum bit error rate of 0.029. Shapley additive explanations explainability analysis validates the contribution of quantum-secure and quantum-safe components to trustworthy decision-making. The proposed quantum AI-based system provides an efficient, scalable, and highly secure solution for future intelligent low-altitude remote sensing systems.
item.authors: Wajdan Al Malwi;Hussam Al Hamadi;Abdulrahman Mohammed Alamoudi;Nazik Alturki;Fatima Asiri;Fahad Masood;

item.title: Multihierarchical Mixed Cube Attention Interactive Network for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
item.description: To address the tradeoff between the spectral resolution and spatial resolution of hyperspectral images (HSIs), hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HSI-MSI) aims to generate a high-spatial-resolution hyperspectral image (HR-HSI) by integrating the spectral information of a hyperspectral image with the spatial details of a corresponding multispectral image (MSI). However, most existing methods overlook the inherent correlation between the spatial and spectral dimensions, limiting their joint exploitation of spatial and spectral information. In this study, a multihierarchical mixed cube attention interactive network (MMCAI-Net) is proposed, which considers this correlation and enhances the deep interaction across spatial and spectral dimensions in the HSI-MSI fusion process. The network primarily consists of a multihierarchical feature interaction stage and a gradual feature reconstruction stage, which are composed of the mixed cube attention interaction (MCAI) and cube feature aggregation and reconstruction (CFAR) modules, respectively. The MCAI module integrates global spatial and spectral information from the HSI and MSI through mixed cube attention, enabling cross-dimensional feature interaction. The CFAR module progressively aggregates these features to reconstruct an HR-HSI with enhanced spatial details and spectral fidelity. Experimental results on five datasets demonstrate that the MMCAI-Net method preserves more spatial and spectral details than seven literature methods, improving PSNR by 5% and reducing SAM by 8% compared with MCT-Net. These results suggest that the proposed method achieves superior HSI-MSI fusion results.
item.authors: Huajing Wu;Wenjing Zhang;Kefei Zhang;Shuangshuang Shi;Fei Zhao;Lin Zhang;Lorenzo Bruzzone;

item.title: FireAURA-Net: Progressive Candidate-Aware Representation and Localization for Tiny Forest-Fire Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
item.description: Detecting tiny forest fire points in remote sensing imagery is challenging due to their low pixel occupancy, weak responses, irregular boundaries, and similarity to fire-like woodland backgrounds. Limited task-specific training data further exacerbate representation insufficiency and foreground–background imbalance. In this article, we propose an adaptive unified response alignment network for tiny forest-fire detection (FireAURA-Net), a lightweight detector. Local-context contrast-guided response mining preserves weak candidates through local-context contrast, shallow spatial guidance, and sparse top-$k$ selection. HSV–Semantic Heterogeneous Representation Collaborative Fusion exploits the consistency and discrepancy between an explicit HSV color prior and candidate semantic responses to improve candidate reliability under fire-like interference. Candidate-localization consistency-guided selective localization refinement block establishes bidirectional interaction between fine-grained candidate cues and deep localization semantics for cross-level refinement. Adaptive dual-cue dynamic reweighting combines target-scale and high-response background cues with weight ramp-up and a batch-level budget constraint to stabilize classification under foreground sparsity. Among the compared methods, FireAURA-Net achieves the highest $\text{AP}$, $\text{AP}_{75}$, and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.193, 0.091, and 0.149, respectively, on forest imagery for remote sensing evaluation of small fire targets, and the highest $\text{AP}_{75}$ and $\text{AP}_{\mathrm{s}}$ of 0.669 and 0.418, respectively, on UAVs-FFDB. These results demonstrate competitive overall detection performance and consistent advantages in detection at $\text{IoU}=0.75$ and in small-scale fire-point detection. Ablation experiments further support the modules' contributions.
item.authors: Yuhan Liu;Hongyang Zhao;Tao Jiang;Jiayi Sun;Yi Liu;Jing Jin;

item.title: LPFI-Net: A Fusion Network for LiDAR Prior and Frequency Interaction in Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification
item.description: The integration of multisource information from hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides reliable data support for land cover classification. The heterogeneity between HSI and LiDAR data poses significant challenges for cross-modal feature alignment, while the rich structural priors inherent in LiDAR data remain underutilized. Therefore, significant feature alignment learning between HSI and LiDAR, together with the embedding of LiDAR structural priors, can substantially improve land cover classification performance. Based on these, we propose the LiDAR prior and frequency interaction network (LPFI-Net). LPFI-Net employs frequency-domain feature learning to achieve flexible HSI-LiDAR salient feature alignment. A frequency-domain interaction mechanism, together with a frequency-invertible enhancement module, is introduced to strengthen cross-band representations and improve HSI-LiDAR feature reconstruction. In the spatial–frequency fusion stage, a LiDAR structural prior-guided mechanism transforms spatial information into quantifiable priors, enabling more effective cross-modal feature enhancement. Experiments on the Houston2013, MUUFL, and Augsburg datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of LPFI-Net, with code available online.
